title: Billing Insights Rollup Engine: per-route/model/customer cost & latency breakdown
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The Console needs accurate, low-latency breakdowns of token cost and per-request latency for each route, model, and customer. Current telemetry is stored as event streams (in Kafka) and raw records in our data lake, but queries for granular rollups are slow and expensive. Goal: build a standalone rollup/aggregation service ("Billing Insights Rollup Engine") that materializes cost and P50/P95/P99 latency breakdowns per-route, per-model, and per-customer across multiple time windows (1m, 5m, 1h, 1d).

Scope and constraints:
- Inputs: normalized request events from Kafka topic 'telemetry.requests', and model-cost metadata from pricing service (REST).
- Outputs: fast read APIs for Console dashboards and chargeback system; scheduled materialized tables for downstream billing exports.
- SLA: dashboard reads should return <200ms for common queries (single customer, single route, last 30d with pre-aggregated window).
- Storage must support efficient incremental updates and point-in-time backfill for schema changes.
- Must integrate with existing cost attribution rules and handle exceptions (overrides, credits).

High-level design (decisions made so far):
1) Hybrid streaming + batch: use a streaming aggregation worker (Flink/Beam) for near-real-time 1m/5m windows, and a nightly batch job to re-aggregate 1h/1d windows and reconcile drift. Rationale: streaming keeps dashboards fresh; nightly job fixes late-arriving events and simplifies retention logic.
2) Materialized store: use ClickHouse for time-series rollups keyed by (customer_id, route_id, model_id, window_start, window_granularity). ClickHouse chosen for analytic read performance and efficient TTLs.
3) Cost attribution: join request events with pricing metadata at aggregation time; pricing changes are snapshots stored in a small metadata table and applied via versioned join keys.
4) Delta updates and replays: implement idempotent aggregates using event sequence offsets + per-key last-processed-offset markers to allow safe replays and partial backfills.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pre-aggregation vs on-the-fly compute: Pre-agg reduces read latency and cost but increases storage/complexity for replays. We chose pre-agg for dashboard SLOs.
- ClickHouse vs BigQuery: ClickHouse provides sub-200ms reads for the target card, BigQuery is cheaper at scale for ad-hoc; we will route ad-hoc queries to BigQuery exports.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Billing+Insights+Rollup+Design (initial draft).
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4256 (streaming worker + ClickHouse schema).
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1b2c-billing-insights-ui (early UX).

Operational concerns:
- Backpressure: streaming worker must apply circuit breakers if ClickHouse ingestion falls behind; metrics and automated alerts required.
- Cost: monitor incremental storage footprint and query costs; provide per-customer quotas for rollups in Dedicated clusters.
- Correctness: nightly reconciliation job includes checksum comparisons and alerting for >0.5% divergence vs raw counts.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming worker consumes telemetry.requests and produces 1m and 5m aggregates into ClickHouse with end-to-end latency <90s for 95% of events
Materialized tables supporting queries by (customer_id, route_id, model_id, window) and returning results <200ms for typical dashboard cards
Nightly reconciliation job re-computes 1h/1d aggregates and corrects streaming drift; post-run divergence <0.1% vs raw counts
APIs for Console read endpoints implemented and documented; includes parameterized filters and pagination
Idempotent ingestion using event-offset markers to allow safe replays and partial backfills
Integration tests covering pricing metadata changes and override handling (unit+integration), green in CI
Runbook created: ingest health metrics, recovery steps for replay, and contact list for on-call owners
